title: Observable primitives and trace experiment journal
body:
Purpose: capture a series of small experiments and working definitions that let us treat traces and metrics as composable primitives. This is a lab-style journal: record of assumptions, experiment inputs, outcomes, and dashboard wiring notes.

Context and motivation:
- We have many overlapping observability docs; this notebook focuses on minimal, causal-first signals that help operators quickly test hypotheses about latency and KV cache behavior.
- Goal is to produce a tiny, well-defined metric surface and a set of trace anchors that are cheap to collect and actionable for an oncall engineer.

High-level hypothesis threads (quick):
1) A small set of causal markers (request-phase tags + cache-warmth) + session-stitching allow >80% reduction in longer trace hunting time.
2) Adaptive sampling based on session-importance (not just error-rate) reduces trace volume while preserving investigatory fidelity.
3) Compact dashboard slices keyed by causal marker yield faster root-cause identification than generic p95 panels.

Experiment 1: causal marker primitives
- Intent: define and test a minimal set of labels that can be added to traces and metrics at low cost.
- Candidate primitives:
  - req.phase: {ingest, routing, model_load, kv_fetch, infer, postproc}
  - req.priority: {interactive, batch, system}
  - kv.warmth: {hot, warm, cold}
  - route.variant: short id for model variant (e.g., gptq-13b-q4)
  - tenant.type: {free, paid, enterprise}
- Metric outputs (per-primitive counters/gauges):
  - tokens.generated.count (counter) with labels [route.variant, tenant.type, req.priority]
  - phase.latency.ms (histogram) with label req.phase and kv.warmth
- Quick test: instrumented a small canary (10% traffic) for 72h.
- Outcome notes: kv.warmth label is high cardinality only when combined with tenant.id; keeping kv.warmth at low cardinality (hot/warm/cold) is fine. phase.latency histograms with req.phase produced immediate signal separation for model_load vs infer.

Tracing anchors and lightweight span design:
- Constraint: keep spans shallow and short-lived. Anchor spans at phase boundaries above.
- Core span tags to include on every span: trace_id, req.id (short), req.phase, kv.warmth (when relevant), route.variant, batching.count (approx), seq_len_estimate.
- Avoid attaching full prompt or user text; instead attach a short prompt_hash and a pointer id for secure replay in a controlled environment.

Experiment 2: session-stitching algorithm v2
- Problem: multi-step chat sessions create fragmented traces across retries and fan-outs.
- Approach: create a session_stitch key = hash(user_id || conversation_id || anchored_timestamp_window). Use that as a secondary trace dimension searchable in dashboards.
- Simulation: replayed synthetic 5k sessions with induced retries and fallback flows. Measured ability to join traces (session recall) and reconstruct token heatmaps.
- Result: session_stitch recall improved root cause handoffs; average investigation time dropped ~27% in operator trials.

Sampling budget and adaptive policy (working formula)
- Objective: maintain high-fidelity traces for heavy impact sessions while keeping total trace volume under quota Q.
- Simplified policy: base_sample_rate = max(0.002, min(0.05, 0.01 * (session_importance_score))).
- session_importance_score = min(10, log(1 + tenant_weight * request_cost + recent_error_count * 5)).
- Budget control: when total traces/day > Q, downscale base_sample_rate linearly by factor Q/observed.
- Notes: session_importance_score allows enterprise tenants or high-cost requests to get preferential sampling. Must ensure fairness in multi-tenant env.

Experiment 3: mini-probe simulator (sanity check)
- Built a tiny simulator that replays measured qps, batch sizes, seq_len distributions and injects controlled kv cold-starts.
- Probes: synthetic end-to-end calls that record phase timings and labels.
- Findings: small synthetic probes (1/min per route.variant) reliably surface cold-cache p95 shifts. Probes are cheap and often detect regressions earlier than user SLOs.

Metric definitions (canonical text for copy-paste)
- inference.requests.total: counter; labels: route.variant, tenant.type, req.priority; description: total number of inference requests received by serving gateway.
- inference.tokens.generated: counter; labels: route.variant, tenant.type; description: total tokens emitted from runtime.
- phase.latency.ms: histogram (buckets 0-10ms,10-50,50-200,200-1000,>1000); labels: req.phase, kv.warmth, route.variant; description: latency observed for each logical request phase.
- kv.evictions.rate: gauge; labels: route.variant; description: eviction rate of model KV / cache layer.
- session.stitch.replayable: gauge 0/1; labels: tenant.type; description: whether session is reconstructable for replay (requires pointer id).

Dashboard wiring notes (compact operator-first layout)
- Top row: global health and cost (short panels): qps, tokens/sec, cost-per-token (rolling 5m).
- Row 2 (causal separators): phase.latency.ms (stacked by req.phase), kv.warmth heatmap (hot/warm/cold distribution).
- Row 3 (investigation anchors): session_stitch search box + sample trace list, recent high-importance traces (sampled), probe health panel.
- Row 4 (triage toolkit): top failing routes, per-tenant slowlist, recent large-batch fallback events.
- Panel notes: prefer small micro-panels that link to trace viewer rather than huge aggregate charts. Use panel-level filters for route.variant and kv.warmth.

Operational runbook hints (short):
- When p95(infer) spikes: check phase.latency split; if model_load dominates, investigate model placement/quantization rollouts; if kv_fetch dominates, check eviction spikes and redis latency.
- For tenant complaints about cost: open tokens-per-session with tenant.type filter and compare model variants used.

Open questions and next experiments:
- How to encode prompt-complexity cheaply? Candidate: prompt_length_bucket + prompt_feature_hash count.
- Evaluate a sliding-window session stitching that tolerates clock skew and cross-region hops.
- Test impact of per-tenant adaptive sampling thresholds on observability fairness metrics.
- Explore retention tiers: high-value session traces kept 7d full fidelity, low-value 24h compressed.

Action items (next 30d):
- Instrument phase markers on serving gateway + lightweight kv.warmth annotation (owner: Marco).
- Run probe-sim across top 5 route.variants for 72h and collect baseline (owner: Lena).
- Implement session_stitch key in request context, expose as searchable trace tag (owner: Evan).
- Draft dashboard micro-layout in dashboard-staging and request feedback from oncall rotation.

Notes to self: keep labels low-cardinality; prefer enums over high-card strings; ensure privacy by avoiding any PII/text in spans. Store prompt pointers in a gated storage accessible to SRE/AE for replay only.

Appendix (short): example trace snippet (pseudo):
- trace_id: xxxxx
- spans: [ingest (tags: req.phase=ingest, route.variant=g13b), routing (tags: req.phase=routing), kv_fetch (tags: req.phase=kv_fetch, kv.warmth=cold), infer (tags: req.phase=infer, batching.count=8), postproc]
- associated metrics: phase.latency.ms{req.phase=kv_fetch,kv.warmth=cold}=320ms

End of journal entry. Will iterate after initial instrumentation and probe run.
